title: Runtime output regression assertor for interleaved tool chains
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Scope:
Create a CI-grade regression assertor that validates output fidelity across streaming transports and tool/function calling adapters when responses are interleaved with partial JSON chunks. The assertor will focus on three failure modes: (1) structural drift (partial/malformed JSON), (2) semantic regression (function-call argument changes), and (3) runtime adapter incompatibilities (HTTP/WS/grpc/edge shim differences).

Goals:
- Produce a deterministic corpus of golden prompts and expected canonical outputs for each supported runtime adapter and model variant.
- Implement a test harness that can replay multiplexed streams (simulating interleaved tool responses and partial chunks) and assert idempotent parsing and function-call semantics.
- Differential test variants that run against previous runtime revisions and current HEAD to surface regressions.
- CI integration with flaky-tolerant gating: failures escalate to flakes vs hard regressions based on historical pass rates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can replay 500 golden prompt scenarios under HTTP, WebSocket streaming, and gRPC streaming adapters with deterministic seeds.
- At least 40 distinct tool/function-call interleaving patterns covered (including nested tool calls and mid-stream tool fallback events).
- Tests run in CI with <5% flakiness rate measured over 5 consecutive runs; flaky tests must be annotated and tracked as follow-ups.
- Automated diff report produced for each CI run with links to failing golden prompt seeds and a per-test fingerprint (anchor text + token-level diff).

Approach / Implementation notes:
1) Corpus: generate a seeded golden-prompt bank (JSONL) with metadata: model_target, adapter, expected_function_calls (canonicalized), expected_structured_json. Store in GCS bucket and mirror a read-only Drive folder for reviewers.
2) Harness: build a lightweight runner in Go (to reuse existing runtime clients) that can simulate partial-chunk emission ordering, network jitter, and tool response latency. The runner will capture reconstructed outputs and compare against canonical outputs using both structural equality (JSON schema tolerant) and semantic equivalence (function-call args normalized).
3) Fingerprinting: derive a compact fingerprint per prompt that captures the canonical token sequence, normalized function-call signature, and a checksum of ordered JSON fields to make triage easier.
4) CI: integrate into nightly canary pipeline and pull-request smoke check. Use historical pass-rate service to mark flakes and create automated issue templates for reproducible failures.
5) Backcompat: provide a compatibility matrix mapping runtime features (prefix caching, kv-cache priming, chunk coalescing) to test cases so regressions can be triaged to kernel/runtime changes vs client adapters.

Risks / Tradeoffs:
- Determinism vs realism: seeding and strict timeouts reduce flakiness but may underrepresent real-world network variability. We'll include a separate "chaos" bucket of non-deterministic stress cases for manual runs.
- Maintenance cost: golden corpus requires periodic refresh as new models are onboarded. We'll add guardrails to auto-detect when a new model variant is mapped and create an auto-PR to seed new golden prompts.

Operational / Triage playbook:
- CI failure produces an artifact with: raw capture, replayer script, fingerprint, and a suggested blame shard (client adapter vs runtime kernel diffs).
- First responders: on-call runtime eng -> triages kernel-level regressions; adapter owners get notified via CODEOWNERS mapping; flake manager annotates flaky tests.

Notes about compatibility layers:
- Tests intentionally exercise the adapter compatibility shim (e.g., JSON framing differences between ws and grpc) and will assert that higher-level function-call contracts remain identical even if low-level chunking differs.

2025-02-14 - Carlos Mendes: Added 8 complex nested tool-call scenarios (including tool fallback mid-stream). Observed non-deterministic ordering in gRPC shim causing 2 failures; created ENG-10438 to track shim hardening.

2025-02-18 - Maya Patel: CI integration PR opened. Initial run shows 11 failing cases; 7 are due to timeouts in the test runner when simulating high jitter. Tuned timeouts and re-ran (pass rate 94% on local reproducible run).

2025-02-24 - Security Review: Requested review for golden prompt storage and PII checks. Ensured corpus contains synthetic-only prompts; security requested an annual audit. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-02-28 - Carlos Mendes: Merged harness core library. Nightly canary scheduled. Created follow-up ENG-10503 to add automated issue template for hard regressions and to wire CODEOWNERS alerts.
